tags: why do dogs bark in their sleep
script: Your dog is stretched out, eyes closed, paws twitching, and suddenly a muffled little bark escapes. They're almost certainly dreaming. Dogs go through the same sleep stages that people do, including REM sleep, which is when most dreaming happens. Brain studies suggest dogs may replay parts of their day, like chasing a ball, meeting a friend or exploring a smell, and the twitches, whimpers and soft barks are their body reacting to the dream. Puppies and senior dogs often dream more visibly, since puppies are processing so many new experiences. During REM sleep, the body is usually relaxed, but small signals can leak through, which is why you see running paws or tiny woofs. Most of the time, it's best to simply let them sleep, since waking a dreaming dog can startle them and sometimes cause a reflex snap. If your dog seems to be having a distressing nightmare, call their name softly from a distance rather than touching them. And if the movements are violent, long-lasting or happen while they seem awake, check with your vet. Otherwise, it's one of the cutest little windows into your dog's inner life.
